response, dropping any picked mark whose product/machine cell no longer exists or no longer has a
positive quantity to pick. An unchanged machine selection with only a product-filter change never
re-requests the projection - `visibleProducts()` simply filters the already-fetched
`pickListProducts` by `appliedProductIds` - so product filtering stays client-side and picked marks
for filtered-out rows are preserved, not dropped, since the underlying cells are still valid and only
hidden from view. Applying an empty staged machine selection clears the matrix locally without calling
the backend, the same as it did before this issue. Products defaults to every product id staged and
applied (so the initial trigger reads "All products" and the matrix starts unfiltered); Machines
defaults to no ids staged or applied, so the page still requires an explicit Apply before it fetches
anything. The Selected Machines chips remain as a read-only summary of `appliedMachineIds`; removing a
chip updates both the applied and staged machine selections (so the dropdown reflects the removal too)
and, since issue #996, drops only that machine's planning work without re-reading the snapshot (see
[Plan picks and Record refill](#plan-picks-and-record-refill-issue-996)). Reset
clears both the staged and applied Products/Machines selections back to those same defaults, along
with the matrix data, `pickedCells`, the overrides, the live filters and the snapshot timestamp,
after confirming when there is planning work to lose (issue #996) - and, since issue #1021, the
copy this tab holds.

**Matrix table layout.** (Issue #996 adds a site header row above this one, a left-sticky Product
column and machine columns of at least 15rem; see [Plan picks and Record
refill](#plan-picks-and-record-refill-issue-996).) The matrix lives in one bounded scroll area (`max-h-[70vh] overflow-auto`),
so a long product list scrolls vertically inside the card while many machine columns still scroll
horizontally in the same area. Every header cell - Product, MDB Code, Storage Qty, Total to Pick and
each applied machine column (issue #496 added MDB Code; issue #885 added Storage Qty) - is
individually `sticky top-0` with an opaque background and a z-index above the body cells,
so the whole header row stays visible while rows scroll under it without showing through. The
`<thead>` element itself, the filter panel and the Selected Machines card are deliberately not
sticky. Sticky positioning does not participate in table column sizing, so header and body keep
identical column widths. The separator between header and body is the opaque `md-gray-100` table-head
surface itself, as in every other #410 table: a collapsed border between `<thead>` and `<tbody>`
scrolls away with the body, and #410 defines no shadow token for a sticky header rule, so the header
cells carry no shadow (issue #417).

**Client-side Product/MDB Code sorting (issue #718).** The Product and MDB Code headers are each a
`<button type="button">` calling `sortBy(column)`, using the same shared `nextSortState`/
`sortAriaState`/`sortColumnLabel`/`compareSortValues` helpers
(`frontend/inventory-app/src/app/components/shared/sortable-column.ts`, issue #583) as the Products
and Needs Ordering tables: the first click on a header sorts ascending, a second click reverses it,
and clicking the other header starts that one ascending. The active header's `[attr.aria-sort]`
reflects `ascending`/`descending` (`none` otherwise) and its visible label gains the
`(ascending)`/`(descending)` suffix. Product sorts by `productName` as locale-aware,
case-insensitive text; MDB Code sorts by the row-level `PickListProduct.mdbCode` numerically. A
product with `mdbCode === null` (shown as "—") always sorts last regardless of direction, the same
page-local null policy Needs Ordering uses for its own missing values - this placement, and the
relative order of two missing-code rows, does not flip with direction, only the order of the
non-missing values does. Ties (equal or both-missing codes, or equal names) fall back to
`productName`, then `productId`, so the order is deterministic. The sort is a derived view computed
inside `visibleProducts()`: it never mutates `pickListProducts`, composes with the existing applied
Products filter, and leaves `pickedCells`, totals and progress figures unchanged. `sortColumn`/
`sortDirection` live only on the component instance - the same as every other piece of page state
here - so the chosen sort survives Apply (including a machine-selection refetch) and chip removal,
but Reset clears it back to no active column, and the next loaded pick list appears in backend order.
No other column (Storage Qty, Total to Pick, the per-machine columns) is sortable, and sorting never
calls an endpoint or introduces a query parameter.

#### Manual pick-list entry and mode selection (issue #744)

Issue #744 (parent #329 child H2) gives the Pick List a second view - manual entry - and the
page-level logic that decides which one is offered. It is the frontend of [Batch refill from the
pick list](#batch-refill-from-the-pick-list-issue-743) above: the read-only calculated matrix never
called a mutation endpoint, so without a usable provider the page had nothing to offer at all; this
issue is what lets a business with no provider, or whose Nayax account has not granted the
calculated list's permissions, still record what it took out of storage.

**Two views, one component each, composed by `PickListComponent`.** `ManualPickListComponent`
(`frontend/inventory-app/src/app/components/pick-list/manual-pick-list.component.ts`) is a dedicated
feature component per the [page composition boundary](#page-composition-boundary-issue-191) rule,
not UI grown inside the page: it owns its own search/category filter state, its "Taken" entries, its
per-row and request-level refusal messages, and the save itself, and is handed the page's own
already-fetched active product list (`PickListComponent.allProducts` - the same list the calculated
view's Products filter already reads) through an `@Input() products`, rather than fetching it a
second time. A successful save emits `@Output() refillRecorded`, which the page answers by
re-fetching that list, so the manual table's storage quantities reflect the refill it just recorded.
`PickListComponent.mode` (`'calculated' | 'manual'`) decides which one is shown.

**A mode switch never destroys manual entry, because manual entry is the only view here that
writes.** What stops a retry deducting the same storage twice is the exact row set and idempotency
key `ManualPickListComponent` keeps (see **Idempotency** below), and that protection lives in the
component instance. So the page creates it once, the first time manual mode is shown
(`manualViewCreated`), and **hides rather than destroys** it afterwards - `[hidden]="mode !==
'manual'"` on the element, the same treatment `MachineDetailComponent` gives its tab panels - so the
typed quantities, the per-row refusals and the key all survive every later switch. Destroying it
instead is a double-deduction path, not a cosmetic loss: an operator whose save ended uncertain could
switch views, find an empty form, retype the same pick and send it under a **new** key, which the
server has no way to recognise as the same refill. Two further rules close the rest of that gap: an
uncertain outcome raises `unresolvedSubmission`, an inline notice that stays on screen until a later
Save resolves it rather than only the toast that fades, and while a save is actually in flight
(`ManualPickListComponent.saveInFlightChange` → `PickListComponent.manualSaveInFlight`) switching
back to calculated is refused outright - the Calculated button is disabled and `switchMode
('calculated')` is a no-op - so no response can land on a view the operator has already left. A page
that never enters manual mode never builds it at all, so the calculated-only path is unchanged. The
calculated matrix needs none of this: it is a read-only projection with nothing to lose, and its
already-fetched state survives simply because nothing clears it.

**The page says what it does to inventory per mode.** The note
(`data-testid="pick-list-inventory-impact"`) states, while Plan picks (the calculated view) is
showing, that it is planning only and that adjusted quantities and ticks stay in the browser and
change no stock (`PLAN_PICKS_INVENTORY_IMPACT`; before issue #996 it called the view read-only). In
Record refill (manual mode) it says instead that nothing is recorded until Record refill is clicked
and that recording reduces each product's storage quantity by the quantity taken
(`RECORD_REFILL_INVENTORY_IMPACT`).
Describing a view that writes `MachineRefill` movements as read-only is the one thing that line must
never do, so both wordings are asserted in `pick-list.component.manual-rendering.spec.ts`.

**When the calculated view is offered, and when it is not.** `PickListComponent.
calculatedUnavailableReason` is the one sentence saying why - empty while the calculated view is a
real choice. It is non-empty for either of the acceptance criteria's two triggers, both read through
the shared `ProviderAvailabilityService` (issue #728, see [Shared provider availability and
error-versus-empty states](#shared-provider-availability-and-error-versus-empty-states-issue-728)):
the existing `machineFleet` unavailability (`machinesUnavailable`, unchanged from before this issue)
for no usable provider at all, and a new `machineStock` permission refusal
(`machineProductsUnavailable`) for a usable provider that has not granted the per-machine product
read the calculated matrix's fan-out needs. The `machineStock` check happens twice, like every other
provider-optional screen's two-stage check: once up front in `ngOnInit`, from `featureAvailability
('machineStock')`, so a permission this session already knows is refused opens the page straight into
manual mode before anything is requested; and again live, in `fetchOrClear`'s `catchError`, through
`ProviderAvailabilityService.noteRefusal` - the same path `loadProviderList` already uses for the
machine fleet - because the calculated matrix's own fan-out (`GetMachineProductsAsync` per selected
machine) is the first concrete read of that permission for a session that has not tried before. A
request failure that is **not** one of the two published Nayax availability codes (a transport
failure, an unrelated `5xx`) stays the existing generic "Failed to load the pick list" toast and does
not force manual mode, because it says nothing about whether the calculated view could work. Non-empty
`calculatedUnavailableReason` forces `mode` to `'manual'` and hides the calculated/manual toggle
entirely (`switchMode('calculated')` is a no-op while it is set) - the same "a control over something
that cannot exist is not shown" rule issue #728 already established, reused here for a whole view
rather than one filter. **A connected business with every permission granted sees no change at all**:
`mode` defaults to `'calculated'`, the toggle is offered, and every existing calculated-mode test
(`pick-list.component.spec.ts`, `pick-list.component.provider-optional.spec.ts`) passes unmodified.

**No local id is ever substituted for a provider one.** The calculated view's own machine selection
is untouched by this issue: it keeps selecting and querying by the raw provider machine id
(`Machine.machineID`) it always has, and manual entry never reads or writes that selection. The batch
refill contract already treats an absent machine as a valid whole-business pick
(`PickListRefillPolicy.ValidateAgainstState` only checks a machine when one is named), which is what
made the machine-free slice this section otherwise describes releasable before any local-machine
selection existed for manual entry at all.

**An optional local machine selector (issue #794 - the second half of G2b, which issue #746 split off
when it took the stock and expense screens onto the local machines; see [Machine fields from the
business's own machines](#machine-fields-from-the-businesss-own-machines-issue-746)) lets manual
entry attribute a pick to one of the business's own machines, with or without a provider.**
`ManualPickListComponent` reads `LocalMachineService.getAll()` (`/api/local-machines`, the same local
records issue #740/#741 gave the stock and expense screens, never a provider id) and offers the
result as **active** local machines by `LocalMachine.name` - shown at all only once that read
succeeds with at least one active machine (`machineSelectorShown`); a business with none, or whose
read is still outstanding, behaves exactly as the machine-free slice above describes. A failed read
(`machinesLoadFailed`) is reported in the selector's place rather than hidden silently, but a save
without a machine still works, exactly as a business with none recorded would. It is never sent to
`PickListService.get`, the calculated view's own machine read, which keeps using provider machine ids
untouched by this selection. **Issue #794's single `selectedMachineId` `<select>` is what issue #904
replaced with the machine matrix below**, which is also where the chosen machines now reach the
server: a pick that names any machine is a multi-machine batch, so the single-machine endpoint's
request-level `machineId` is no longer sent by this frontend at all.

**The machine-page consolidation the 18 October 2026 owner decision describes - replacing the
machine-detail page's per-product quantity inputs with a link into this screen, with that machine
preselected as its one machine column - is issue #744's own later phase**; see
[Machine-page consolidation: the "Record refill" link](#machine-page-consolidation-the-record-refill-link-issue-744)
below.

**The machine matrix: one column per selected machine, one request per Save (issue #904).** The
machine selection is `selectedMachineIds` - the shared `MultiSelectDropdownComponent` over
`machineOptions()`, in the operator's own selection order, which is also the column order - and it is
what chooses between the screen's **two modes, one per endpoint**:

- **No machine selected** is issue #744's machine-free entry, unchanged: one "Taken" column, saved
  through `PickListService.recordRefill` (`POST /api/pick-list/refills`) with no `machineId` at all.
- **One or more machines selected** renders Product, Category, Storage Qty, **Total Taken** - the
  row's own sum across the selected machines - and then one quantity column per machine, and one Save
  sends the whole run through `PickListService.recordMultiMachineRefill`
  (`POST /api/pick-list/multi-machine-refills`, see [Multi-machine refill batch](#multi-machine-refill-batch-issue-897))
  as a single batch of `(machineId, productId, quantityTaken)` allocations in catalogue-then-column
  order. **Never one request per machine**: each product's allocations come off one shelf, and only
  one request can weigh their total against it inside the write lock - which is the reason that
  endpoint exists. A single selected machine is a one-column matrix and takes the same path, so the
  retry and attribution rules below do not change shape with the size of the selection.

**Drafts are per mode, and nothing is silently reassigned, copied or dropped.** The "No machine"
entries (`takenById`, by product) and the matrix cells (`cellValues`, by product **and** machine) are
separate drafts; a generic quantity is never written into every selected column, because that would
invent a pick several times the size of the one that was typed. A selection change that would drop a
typed quantity therefore asks first - `DISCARD_UNATTRIBUTED_ENTRIES_CONFIRMATION` on the way into
machine columns, `DISCARD_MACHINE_COLUMNS_CONFIRMATION` on the way back out, and
`discardMachineColumnConfirmation(...)`, which names the columns, when some of them are removed - and
**Cancel changes nothing at all**, neither the selection nor one entry (`window.confirm`, the same
confirmation `MachineDetailComponent` and the Admin workflows use). A confirmed removal drops exactly
the removed columns' cells, so re-adding a machine brings back an empty column rather than a
discarded quantity. The search and category filters never touch a draft at all: they hide rows, and a
hidden row's entries are still validated, still sent, and still counted in `totalUnitsRequired()` -
which is why `hiddenUnitsRequired()`/`hiddenProductsWithEntries()` are shown beside it rather than
leaving an operator to discover a hidden row from a refusal. The one place an entry changes column is
the preselected machine's own window, below.

**Per-cell validation, and what blocks Save.** `parseTakenEntry` is the one rule for every box in
both modes: blank or `0` is nothing taken, a positive whole number up to `MAXIMUM_TAKEN_QUANTITY`
(the server's `int`) is a quantity, and anything else - negative, fractional, nonnumeric, or larger
than the server can record (`TAKEN_QUANTITY_TOO_LARGE_MESSAGE`) - is refused inline on its own cell
and blocks Save, wherever it is. Because a cell is one product on one machine, the blocked Save also
states which: `invalidEntryMessages` names each one as "<product> at <machine>: <message>", including
cells on rows the current filter hides. A `400` from the batch endpoint is parsed by
`parseMultiMachineRefillRejection`, which maps each `allocations[i]` key back to the
**(product, machine)** pair the submitted allocation at that index named - not to a position in the
currently filtered or reordered matrix - so a per-allocation refusal, including the aggregate
"these allocations take N units, but only M are in stock" reported on *every* contributing
allocation, lands on the cells it is about; `idempotencyKey`, `notes` and the bare `allocations` key
surface as request-level messages. A definitive refusal leaves every draft editable.

**Nothing moves while a save is in flight.** `saving` disables every entry box, disables the machine
dropdown (a `<fieldset disabled>` around it, so its trigger and checkboxes go with it) and makes
`onSelectedMachineIdsChange`, `removeMachineColumn`, `onCellChange` and `onTakenChange` return
without doing anything, so the request being answered is the request that was built.

**Entry, validation and the save contract.** Manual entry lists every product in `products` (already
active-only, since `ProductService.getAll()` with no filters answers the working catalogue), with a
client-side, case-insensitive name search and a category filter whose options are derived from the
`category` already nested on each product - not a second `CategoryService.getAll()` call - sorted by
name. Each row's "Taken" box holds free text; a blank box or an explicit `0` means nothing was taken
and contributes no row, and anything else that is not a positive whole number is refused inline with
"Enter a whole number greater than 0." (mirroring `PickListRefillPolicy.QuantityMustBePositiveMessage`
without importing it - a second, Angular-side copy of the same rule, the same way
`business-application-rules.ts` mirrors `BusinessSettingsPolicy`) and blocks Save until it is fixed or
cleared, regardless of whether that row is currently visible under the search/category filter. In the
"No machine" mode Save builds its row set from every product in `products` order (not the
visible/filtered subset) whose "Taken" box parses to a positive quantity, and sends exactly
`{ idempotencyKey, rows }` - no `machineId`, no `notes` - to `PickListService.recordRefill`
(`POST /api/pick-list/refills`); with machine columns it builds allocations instead and sends the
batch described above. A `400`'s
`ValidationProblemDetails` is parsed by `pick-list-refill-errors.ts`'s `parsePickListRefillRejection`:
each `rows[i]` key is mapped back to the **product id** the submitted row at that index named (not
the row's position in the currently-visible, filtered list), so a refusal lands on the right line
however the operator has since re-sorted or re-filtered; any other key (`idempotencyKey`, `machineId`,
`notes`, the bare `rows` key - none of which this screen offers a field for) surfaces as a
request-level message instead. A successful save clears every "Taken" box and toasts "Refill
recorded."; nothing is saved to `localStorage`, a query parameter, or any state outside the component
instance, matching the calculated view's own no-persistence rule.

**Idempotency and the three outcomes a save can have (issue #743's contract, read correctly from the
client side).** `ManualPickListComponent` keeps the exact payload and key of its last attempted save
(`lastSubmission`, which is either a row set for the "No machine" mode or an allocation set for the
matrix) and compares it with what Save would send now:

- **An unchanged resubmission reuses the key and resends the identical payload**, generated nowhere
  else - not even recomputed from the current product order - so a retry is bit-for-bit the same
  request the server last saw, whatever else on screen may have changed (a filter, a sort) in
  between. A batch compares as a **set** of allocations (`multiMachineAllocationsEqual`), so merely
  reordering the machine columns is still the same pick under the same key - which matches the
  server, whose `MultiMachinePickListRefillFingerprint` renders a batch in its own
  machine-then-product order. This is what makes the three failure modes safe to retry at all: the
  request-shape and against-state rules of both endpoints refuse *before* the use case ever claims
  the idempotency key (see [Batch refill from the pick list](#batch-refill-from-the-pick-list-issue-743)
  and [Multi-machine refill batch](#multi-machine-refill-batch-issue-897) above), so a `400` has
  recorded nothing and the same key is always safe to resend once the named row or cell is fixed.
- **A `400` is a definite, per-row refusal.** Nothing was recorded; `rowErrors`/`requestErrors` are
  replaced from the response (never merged with a previous attempt's), and `lastSubmission` is left
  exactly as it is - an unedited retry resends the same refused request, which is deterministic and
  harmless, while editing a flagged row changes the row set and so mints a new key on the next Save.
- **A `409` means the key is already spent on a *different* request.** Reusing it would only be
  refused again, so `lastSubmission` is cleared and the next Save always mints a fresh key; the
  response's own `detail` sentence (`DomainExceptionHandler`'s `ProblemDetails`) is shown, or a
  generic one when it carries none.
- **Anything else (a network failure, an unrelated `5xx`) is uncertain - it is not known whether the
  server recorded the refill before the response was lost.** `lastSubmission` is left untouched and
  the entered quantities are **not** cleared, so the retry resends precisely the same request under
  precisely the same key: if the first attempt had in fact been recorded, the retry is answered as a
  replay and writes nothing a second time; if it had not, the retry records it. Either way the
  operator never has to decide which happened. This is the one outcome that sets
  `unresolvedSubmission`, so the attempt stays reported on screen until a later attempt resolves it,
  and it is why the component survives a mode switch at all; a `400`, a `403` and a `409` are
  definite answers and leave it clear.
- **While an outcome is uncertain, no new key may be minted at all - the kept payload is the only
  request that may be sent (issue #904's tightening of this rule).** The screen offers an explicit
  **Retry save** (`retry()`, `canRetry`) that resends exactly `lastSubmission`, and `save()` *is*
  that retry while `unresolvedSubmission` is set, so an edited cell, a removed machine column or a
  reordered selection cannot turn one physical pick into a second deduction. Before #904, editing a
  quantity after an uncertain outcome minted a new key, which is a second deduction whenever the
  first attempt had in fact committed; a matrix makes that path far easier to walk into, because the
  columns themselves move. A different pick is accepted again only once that attempt has a definite
  answer - which one Retry always produces, since every outcome other than another uncertain one
  resolves it.
- **A `403` is a definite refusal too** - a read-only support session, or a capability the member
  lacks, refused the request before anything was recorded - so it is reported as a refusal ("This
  refill was refused, so nothing was recorded.", or the response's own `detail`), never as the
  uncertain outcome that asks for a retry, and `lastSubmission` is cleared so a later, permitted Save
  mints its own key.

**A support session is read-only here too (issue #658's rule).** A support session grants
`Inventory.Operate`, so the backend refuses this write only by its read-only method rule. Like
`MachineDetailComponent`'s Restock, `ManualPickListComponent` subscribes to `SupportSessionService.
active$` (`sessionActive`) and, while it is set, **hides** every entry column - the "Taken" column,
and in the matrix the Total Taken and machine columns with it - along with Save, Retry save and the
storage-requirement line, and says why (`data-testid="manual-pick-list-support-session"`); the
product list and storage quantities stay readable. `canSave` is false and `save()` returns before sending, so a session that starts after the
page opened cannot send a refill either. An already-raised uncertain-save notice stays visible.

**The catalogue's own load state.** Manual entry is built entirely from `allProducts`, so an empty
array cannot be read as "no products" until a read has succeeded. `PickListComponent.loadProducts()`
is the one catalogue read - on arrival, after each recorded refill, and on retry - tracked by a
`ListLoadState` (`productsLoadState`) so a superseded response never overwrites a newer one; only the
first successful read seeds the Products filter's selection. It hands manual entry `catalogueState`
(`'loading' | 'failed' | 'loaded'`): while the first read is outstanding the table says "Loading
products…", a failed first read says the list could not be loaded with a **Retry** button, and "No
active products match your filters." is shown only after a successful read. A failed refresh after a
recorded refill (`catalogueRefreshFailed`) keeps the last list, says the storage quantities may be out
of date (`data-testid="manual-pick-list-refresh-failed"`) and offers **Refresh**; either failure also
toasts. `pick-list.component.manual-rendering.spec.ts` covers a delayed first read, a failed first
read and its retry, a successful empty read, and a failed refresh, plus the support-session cases
(no Taken boxes, no Save, no POST and no uncertain-write notice, including a session that starts after
the page opened); `manual-pick-list.component.spec.ts` covers the `save()` guard and the `403` outcome.

**What proves it.** `idempotency-key.spec.ts` (the generator's uniqueness and the 128-character
contract bound), `pick-list-refill-errors.spec.ts` (`rows[i]` mapped back to the submitted row's
product id, `allocations[i]` mapped back to the submitted allocation's product **and** machine,
request-level keys kept separate, `null` for a `409`/network failure/a body with no `errors`, and
`multiMachineAllocationsEqual` treating a reordered batch as the same submission),
`manual-pick-list.component.spec.ts` (filtering, the blank/zero/malformed/too-large entry rules in
both modes, the exact submitted row and allocation sets and their order, the matrix's row and whole-
pick totals including rows a filter hides, every discard confirmation and what Cancel leaves
untouched, the in-flight locks on the selection, the column removals and the cells, the three failure
outcomes above including the idempotency-key reuse/mint rules and that **no** key is minted while an
outcome is uncertain however the matrix is edited, removed from or reordered, that a save in flight is
never resent, and which outcomes leave `unresolvedSubmission` set), `pick-list.component.mode.spec.ts`
(the default calculated mode, both forced-manual triggers -
up front and live - the generic-failure exception, the manual-mode toggle, that switching back to
calculated preserves the already-fetched matrix, that the manual view is created once and kept, and
that manual mode cannot be left while a save is in flight) and
`pick-list.component.manual-rendering.spec.ts` (the toggle and the manual table rendered through the
real template, including the provider-unavailable case hiding the Calculated option entirely, both
mode-specific inventory-impact wordings, an uncertain save retried with the identical key and body
after switching to calculated and back, the toggle refusing to move while a save is in flight, and -
for the matrix - one labelled column per selected machine with the Total Taken column before them,
the bounded scroll container the columns live in, the per-cell error and the product-and-machine
sentence that blocks Save, the whole-pick storage requirement with the part a filter hides, the
confirmed and cancelled column removal, the one batch request a Save sends, and the explicit
**Retry save** resending the identical request after an edit). Also proved in
`pick-list.component.spec.ts`: a manual pick's local machine columns never reach the calculated
view's provider machine ids. Not listed above because it predates this section:
`manual-pick-list.component.spec.ts`'s machine-selection describe block (issue #794) already covers
`machineSelectorShown`, `activeMachines` excluding inactive machines and the failed-read fallback; see
[Machine-page consolidation: the "Record refill" link](#machine-page-consolidation-the-record-refill-link-issue-744)
immediately below for what issue #744's own later phase added on top of it.

#### Machine-page consolidation: the "Record refill" link (issue #744)

The owner's 18 October 2026 decision, finished once issues #743, #744's machine-free manual mode,
#794's machine selector and #746's local machines had all shipped: the machine-detail page's
per-product Restock inputs are **removed**, not merely hidden, and replaced with one **Record
refill** link into the manual pick list this document already describes above, now opened with this
machine preselected. The decision deliberately kept the old inputs in place until every one of those
dependencies existed - a replacement that cannot yet attribute a refill to the right machine is worse
than the thing it would replace - which is why this phase, rather than the machine-free phase above,
is the one that removes them.

**`MachineDetailComponent.restockProduct` and its per-row quantity input/button are gone.** The
Products tab's Actions column is gone with them; `StockService`, `StockAdjustmentReason` and
`StockAdjustmentDto` are no longer imported by this component at all. The column's other two
read-only pieces - the stock badge (`stockClass`, `{{ quantityInStock }} / {{ maxStockInMachine }}`)
and `MachineRestockSyncComponent`'s own Sync Restock section above the tabs - are both untouched;
this phase removes a **write** control, never the stock display.

**The replacement is one link, not a per-row control**, in the Products panel's card header beside
the product count: `routerLink="/pick-list" [queryParams]="{ mode: 'manual', machineId:
machine?.localMachineId }"`. It is rendered only once `machine?.localMachineId` is known (the
`@if (machine$ | async as machine)` block this link already sits inside), and it is **hidden**, not
disabled, while a support session is active - `*ngIf="!sessionActive"` on the link itself, the same
treatment Restock had and `MachineRestockSyncComponent`'s own session guard already gives Sync
Restock - because the write it leads to is refused by `ManualPickListComponent.save`'s own existing
support-session rule (see above), and there is no partial, read-only version of "open the pick list"
to leave reachable.

**`machineId` is always the local machine id, never the raw Nayax number, and that is true by
construction, not by a frontend check.** `machine.localMachineId` on this page is not merely usually
present: `GET api/machines/{id}` (`MachinesController.GetById`) takes the **local** id as its route
parameter and sets `MachineSummary.LocalMachineId` to exactly that id on every response (see the
controller's own `// Every {id} below is a local machine, Machines.Id` comment, issue #741) - the
page's own `machine$` can therefore never carry a `machineID` provider number where a local id is
needed, which is the invariant the issue's "never treat the provider id as a local id" instruction
is about. The link reuses that same already-loaded value; it introduces no new identity resolution.

**`PickListComponent` reads the link's query parameters once, synchronously, in `ngOnInit`** - from
`ActivatedRoute.snapshot.queryParamMap`, a one-shot deep link read rather than a value this page
tracks across its own later navigation. `mode=manual` only chooses the page's **starting** view by
calling the same `setMode('manual')` the manual-mode toggle already calls; it does not force manual
mode the way `calculatedUnavailableReason` does, so a connected business still sees the Calculated
toggle offered and can switch to it, and `calculatedUnavailableReason` and every other calculated-view
rule above are completely unaffected. `machineId` is parsed only as "is this a positive integer" -
this page performs no identity lookup of its own - and becomes `PickListComponent.
preselectedMachineId`, passed into `ManualPickListComponent`'s `@Input` of the same name. Ordinary
navigation to `/pick-list` (the nav menu entry, a bookmark) carries neither query parameter, so
`mode` stays its existing default (`'calculated'`) and `preselectedMachineId` stays `null` - this
phase changes nothing about that path.

**`ManualPickListComponent` is the only place that resolves `preselectedMachineId` against the
business's actual machines**, once its own `LocalMachineService.getAll()` read (issue #794, above)
settles - success or failure alike. A link's machine id is accepted as the real selection, exactly as
if the operator had chosen it from the dropdown, only when it names one of `activeMachines`; this is
also what the issue's "resolve to the current business's local machine" requirement reduces to, since
the id arriving here was already a local id by construction (previous bullet) and the only remaining
question is whether it is still one of *this* business's *active* machines by the time the pick list
loads. It becomes **exactly one** machine column (`selectedMachineIds = [id]`, issue #904) and more
may be added beside it, because a run that starts at one machine is still a run. When it is not -
deactivated or removed between opening the machine page and clicking the link, or the machine read
itself failed - `machineAttributionFailed` is raised instead of silently leaving the selection empty:
the link promised this refill would be attributed to that machine, so a save that quietly went
through as "No machine" would misrepresent what happened. The message
(`data-testid="manual-pick-list-machine-attribution-failed"`) is shown beside the selector rather
than blocking the screen, and the dropdown itself is never forced into a false state - a resolved
preselection is a real, changeable selection, and a failed one leaves the selection exactly where it
already honestly was, so the operator can still pick a machine from the list (if one is shown) or
save explicitly against "No machine".

**Until that resolution settles, Save is refused.** `machineResolutionPending` is `true` exactly
while a link named a machine and the machine read has not answered either way, and both `canSave`
and `save()` refuse while it is. The two reads are independent: `products` is the page's own
already-fetched catalogue, so it is routinely ready first, and without this rule an operator could
type quantities and submit a refill in that window with **no** `machineId` at all - neither the
machine the link promised nor a deliberate "No machine" - and with no attribution warning, because
`machineAttributionFailed` is only decided once the read settles. It also closes the retry
consequence that follows from it: a submission kept for an unchanged retry carries its machine, so a
machine arriving *after* an uncertain first attempt would change what the next Save compares against,
mint a new idempotency key, and let a first request that did commit deduct storage a second time.
Refusing the save until the attribution is known means no request can leave while it is unresolved,
so there is no kept submission for a late answer to change underneath. The wait is announced in the
selector's place (`data-testid="manual-pick-list-machine-resolution-pending"`, `role="status"`) and
the "Taken" boxes stay open, so the operator can keep typing; **ordinary entry never waits**, because
`preselectedMachineId` is `null` and the pending state is never raised at all. A quantity typed in
that window belongs to the one machine the link named - that is what the link and the pending notice
both promised - so when the read answers it **moves into that machine's column** rather than being
dropped or sent unattributed (issue #904). That is the only place an entry changes column, it is
always one machine, and it is never a copy into several; a link whose machine does not resolve leaves
those entries exactly where they are, as the unattributed pick they honestly still are.

**Sync Restock's fallback wording now points at the pick list.** `MachineRestockSyncComponent`'s
description previously said "Manual restocking above remains available as a fallback"; "above" named
a control that no longer exists, so it now says the pick list's manual entry is the fallback instead.
No behaviour changed here - Sync Restock's own reconciliation workflow, duplicate detection and
already-recorded handling (described above in this document) are untouched by this phase.

**Reconciliation already treated a pick-list refill exactly like the removed Restock action, so
nothing had to change for it to keep working.** `RecordPickListRefill`'s own store
(`EfPickListRefillStore.ApplyAsync`) records each row through the same `IRecordInventoryMovement`
movement logic as the removed action did, as `StockAdjustmentReason.MachineRefill` with
`StockAdjustmentSource.Manual` - identical facts, not merely an equivalent effect. Sync Restock's
possible-duplicate detector (`NayaxMachineStockSyncPoliciesTests`,
`MachineStockSyncTests`) matches an unprocessed Nayax stock-adjustment event against existing
`StockAdjustment` rows by machine, product and timing, with no awareness of which UI entry point
created a given `Manual` row; a refill recorded through the Record refill link is therefore already
exactly as eligible for "Already recorded manually" as one recorded through the action it replaced,
and importing the matching Nayax event afterward still cannot deduct the same storage a second time.
This is a regression guarantee this phase verifies, not a new rule it adds.

**What proves it.** `machine-detail.component.spec.ts` covers the Record refill link carrying
`machine.localMachineId` (never `machineID`) as its `machineId` query parameter, the link being
hidden during a support session, and that the removed Restock button and quantity input no longer
render at all. `pick-list.component.mode.spec.ts` covers `mode=manual` opening straight into manual
mode while still offering the Calculated toggle, `machineId` arriving as `preselectedMachineId`, a
malformed `machineId` preselecting nothing, and ordinary navigation with no query parameters being
unaffected. `manual-pick-list.component.spec.ts`'s "machine preselection from a link" describe block
covers a resolved preselection, a deactivated/removed/unreadable-list failure each raising
`machineAttributionFailed` without changing the submitted `machineId`, and no failure being raised
when no machine was linked at all. Three of its tests hold the machine read open on a `Subject` to
cover the window above: Save refused and no request sent while a linked machine is unresolved and
then submitted with its `machineId` once the read answers; ordinary no-machine entry saving
immediately with the read still outstanding; and an uncertain attempt made after the machine resolved
being retried with the identical key, machine and rows, so a late answer can never become a second
deduction.

#### Plan picks and Record refill (issue #996)

Issue #996 redesigns both Pick List views and renames them in the UI - **Plan picks** for the
calculated view (`mode === 'calculated'`) and **Record refill** for manual entry (`mode ===
'manual'`); the internal mode names, routes, query parameters and every API call are unchanged. It is
frontend only: no endpoint, DTO, schema or Nayax call was added or altered, and both views still
compose exactly as described in the two sections above.

**Planning state is transient and keyed per cell.** `PickListComponent` adds `overrides`
(`Map<string, number>`) and keeps `pickedCells` (`Set<string>`), both keyed by `planCellKey(productId,
machineId)` (`frontend/inventory-app/src/app/components/pick-list/plan-picks.ts`). The planned
quantity of a cell is its override when present, otherwise the projection's `quantityToPick`; every
total, shortage and progress figure (`productPlannedTotal`, `productShortage`, `totalToPickUnits`,
`actionableCellCount`, `runProgressLabel`) is computed from planned quantities, never written back.
`parsePickQuantity` is the one input rule: digits only, 0 to `MAXIMUM_PICK_QUANTITY` (int32 max),
blank refused. Only a cell with a positive suggestion is editable. 0 is a skip - the cell has no checkbox and counts as no pick. A value
that differs from the cell's previous planned quantity removes its `pickedCells` mark, because it is
a different pick. None of it reaches `localStorage`, a query parameter or any request; since issue
#1021 it is kept in this browser tab's own `sessionStorage` (see
[Keeping the plan in the browser tab](#keeping-the-plan-in-the-browser-tab-issue-1021) below).

**Every editable cell is edited in place, with no edit mode (issue #1008).** The owner's decision of
30 October 2026 replaced #996's pencil and its confirm/cancel for Plan picks only: the shared
`#pickCell` template now renders, on desktop and on a phone alike, a minus button, an always-visible
`inputmode="numeric"` box and a plus button, with the completion checkbox still in its existing
right-hand position and Current/Target beneath them. There is no committed-versus-editing state and
no `edit` object: `onQuantityInput` validates the **complete** text on every keystroke through the
same `parsePickQuantity`, and a usable quantity is the override at once - no confirm click and no
blur - so totals, shortage indicators and progress follow immediately. `stepQuantity` moves the
effective quantity by exactly one and is bounded by `canDecreaseQuantity`/`canIncreaseQuantity` at 0
and at `MAXIMUM_PICK_QUANTITY`.

Text the plan cannot use is neither coerced nor discarded. It is held in
`invalidQuantities` (`Map<string, InvalidPickQuantity>`, the same cell key) exactly as typed, with
the message refusing it; a blank box is such an incomplete input and never an implicit 0, and an
overflowing value is refused whole rather than clamped. While a cell is in that state its last valid
effective quantity goes on carrying every total, the cell says so inline
(`role="alert"`, referenced by the box's `aria-describedby`, naming the quantity still used), both
steppers and the checkbox are disabled, and `togglePicked`/`canComplete` refuse it - and because any
text differing from the last valid value clears that cell's `pickedCells` mark, an unreadable cell
can never be left looking complete. `useSuggestion` also clears the pending text. A pending
`invalidQuantities` entry is unsaved work exactly as an override is: it counts in
`hasPlanningWork`/`machineHasPlanningWork`, survives search, category, status filtering, sorting, a
Record refill round trip and a changed phone machine focus, and is dropped only by the confirmed
discards below. None of this changes the planning-only boundary: Plan picks still calls nothing but
the read-only `GET /api/pick-list` projection, and no adjustment reaches stock, a target, a refill or
Record refill.

**Discarding is explicit and snapshot-scoped.** Overrides, ticks and pending invalid text belong to
the snapshot they were
made against, so anything that replaces the snapshot discards them after `window.confirm`: `refresh()`
(which re-reads the same `appliedMachineIds`, and is also the Retry of a failed read), `resetAll()`,
and an Apply that adds machines. Removing machines (by chip or by Apply) only filters the snapshot, so
it confirms only when a removed machine has planning work and drops just that machine's keys
(`afterMachinesRemoved`). Every one of those discards clears the stored copy too (issue #1021), and a
cancelled confirmation changes neither the page nor the stored copy. Search, category, the Only
remaining / Only shortages status filter,
sorting and the phone layout's machine focus are derived views in `visibleProducts()` /
`focusedProducts()` and never touch planning state.

##### Keeping the plan in the browser tab (issue #1021)

The owner's decision of 31 October 2026 was to keep a Plan picks plan in the browser rather than on
the server, so leaving the Pick List and coming back no longer warns and then loses it. It remains
frontend only: no endpoint, DTO, schema, Nayax call or stored business data changed, and the plan
never travels in a request.

**Two new files, with one responsibility each.**
`frontend/inventory-app/src/app/components/pick-list/plan-picks-storage.ts` is the only code in the
application that touches the `sessionStorage` entry `inventoryapp.planPicks`: it holds the stored
format (`StoredPlanPicks`, versioned by `PLAN_PICKS_STORAGE_VERSION`), writes it, and validates
everything read back. `plan-picks-store.service.ts` (`PlanPicksStoreService`, root-provided, injected
by `PickListComponent` alone) decides whether anything may be stored or restored at all.

**`sessionStorage`, not `localStorage`.** The plan carries the business's product names and storage
figures, so it is kept in the narrowest storage that survives an in-app navigation and a reload: one
tab, never shared with another tab or device, gone when the tab closes. Sharing a plan between tabs
or devices is deliberately out of scope.

**Eligibility is three questions, and all three must be answered before anything is read.** The
scope is the signed-in identity (`activeAccountKey`, the key every other cached answer in this
application is scoped by) and the business `GET /api/me/access` reports. `unread` access is "not read
yet" and waits; `unavailable`
is a refused or failed capability read and stores and restores nothing. A support session
(`SupportSessionService.active$`) and a role preview (`RolePreviewService.active$`) are both
memory-only contexts by design, and neither writes nor restores a plan. Every distinct scope answer
takes a new token, and a plan read under one is refused by `isCurrentScope` if the identity, the
business or the session context changed while the page was still waiting for its machine list.

**The business name is the first filter on a stored plan, never the proof of whose it is.**
`GET /api/me/access` reports a business **name** and no identifier, and a name is mutable and not
unique: one account whose membership moved to a different business of the same name matches
`PlanPicksScope` exactly. What binds a plan to one business is therefore the fleet read's own
identity for each applied machine - `Machine.localMachineId`, this business's machine record, which
the database assigns and no other business holds (`StoredPlanMachine`). `PickListComponent`
re-verifies it on every restore (`verifiedRestoredMachineIds`): a machine the fleet no longer lists
is dropped as before, a machine the fleet lists under a **different** machine record refuses the
whole record rather than the part that disagrees, and a record whose surviving machines carry no
machine record at all is refused too, because nothing in it can be checked. The same rule applies
symmetrically when writing (`storableMachines`): a run no applied machine of which has a machine
record is **not stored**, and the existing `UNSAVED_WORK_LEAVE_WARNING` goes on protecting it - a
plan is never kept on a guarantee the frontend cannot verify. A business-scoped identifier on
`GET /api/me/access` (for example `businessId`) is the missing contract that would make this exact,
and would also let a same-name membership change be detected while a tab is open; adding it is a
backend change the issue excludes and remains follow-up work.

**A plan is bound to its scope for its whole life, not only until it is restored.** Every plan on
screen carries the scope token it was read or planned under (`PickListComponent.planScopeToken`,
captured when the snapshot is requested or restored), and `PlanPicksStoreService.save(plan,
scopeToken)` requires it: planning work can never be written under a scope that became current after
it was made. `scopeToken$` publishes every change of scope, and the page acts on it at once
(`onScopeToken`/`discardPlanForScopeChange`): a restoration still waiting for the fleet read is
dropped unapplied, and a plan already displayed is discarded with its stored copy, its applied
machine selection and its Products filter, because it holds the previous business's product names
and storage figures and the context now in effect - another account, another business, a started
support session or role preview, capabilities being read again - may not see them. The snapshot
generation is bumped with it, so a `GET /api/pick-list` read in flight for the previous scope cannot
land either. Nothing asks the operator first: there is no longer a context to ask in.

**Nothing read back is trusted.** A stored record is a payload from outside the running application,
so `readStoredPlanPicks` checks the version (`PLAN_PICKS_STORAGE_VERSION`, 2 since the machine
identity above; a version 1 record is discarded, never upgraded), the account and business it names,
and then every machine entry, field, row, cell and `planCellKey` (`isPlanCellKey`) before returning
anything; a record that is
present but unusable is removed rather than answered with. Private mode, a quota and a refused
storage access all surface as throws and are each caught: a failed read is "nothing stored", and a
failed write answers `false` **and** removes the previous record, so an older plan is never left
behind looking like the latest saved work.

**What the page stores and restores.** `PickListComponent.persistPlan()` writes the complete plan -
`appliedMachines` (each with its `localMachineId`, above), `appliedProductIds`, `pickListProducts`,
the snapshot's own `lastRefreshedAt` as
an ISO string, and the `overrides`, `pickedCells` and `invalidQuantities` entries - after every change
to any of them, and `forgetPersistedPlan()` clears it on every discard. `restorePlanWhenReady()`
applies the stored plan once both the stored-plan read and the fleet read have settled, trimmed to
the machines the fleet still lists: a machine that is gone is dropped with its cells and keys, and a
plan with nothing left is ignored and forgotten. Because the snapshot travels with the plan, a
restore makes **no** `GET /api/pick-list` call and keeps the original "last refreshed" instant;
`loadState` is settled without a request. Display state (search, category, status filter, sort, phone
machine focus) is deliberately not restored, a restored plan never seeds Record refill (only the
snapshot's own suggestions reach it, as before), and nothing here touches `mode` or
`preselectedMachineId`, so `?mode=manual&machineId=<id>` still opens Record refill exactly as it did.
Automatically refreshing a restored snapshot, and any "this plan is old" banner, are possible
follow-up work and not in this release.

**Stale responses are dropped by generation.** Each snapshot read captures `snapshotGeneration`
(bumped by every fetch, Reset and empty selection) and the `ListLoadState` token; a response or error
is applied only while both are still current, so an older read finishing after a newer one, or after
Reset, can neither replace the newer snapshot nor show a failure over it.

**Site grouping is optional.** The machine dropdown (`MultiSelectOption.group`) and the matrix's
site header row group machines by site from `SiteService.getList()`, read only when some
machine carries a `siteId`. The matrix groups by `siteId` (`ColumnGroup`), using the name only as the
header label, so two sites that share a name are never merged; machines with no known site fall under "Other machines", and a failed
site read falls back to the ungrouped layout rather than an error.

**Record refill validates the whole submission client-side.** `ManualPickListComponent` computes
each product's total across every selected machine - including rows hidden by search, category or
the Entered filter - against its storage quantity (`storageExcess`, `shortageProducts`). Any shortage
disables a **fresh** submission (`canSave`/`save`) and relabels the button `RESOLVE_SHORTAGE_LABEL`;
the server's own aggregate check (issue #897) remains the authority, this only stops a request that
is certain to be refused. An outstanding `unresolvedSubmission` is never blocked by it: Retry save
resends the identical payload and key whatever the catalogue now says. While `entriesLocked` (a save
in flight or unresolved) every cell edit, stepper, machine change and Clear is refused. Plan picks
quantities are handed to Record refill as `@Input() suggestions` keyed by product and local machine
id (`localMachineId` from the fleet read); entering less than a suggestion is shown as information
only and nothing is copied automatically.

**Leaving the page is guarded.** The `/pick-list` route has `canDeactivate: [confirmPickListLeave]`
(`pick-list-leave.guard.ts`), which asks `PickListComponent.confirmLeave()`; a `window:beforeunload`
listener covers reloads and closed tabs. Both use `leaveWarning()`: a save in flight or unresolved
outranks entered Record refill quantities or planning work. Since issue #1021 planning work warns
only while it is **unsaved** (`unsavedPlanningWork()`): the warning is withheld once
`persistPlan()` has actually stored the complete plan, and anything that leaves it unstored - a
refused write, a run whose business identity cannot be verified, a scope that moved on - leaves
`planPersisted`
false so the existing `UNSAVED_WORK_LEAVE_WARNING` goes on asking - the no-warning claim is
conditional on a successful write, never on one having been attempted. Record refill is unchanged:
typed quantities still give `UNSAVED_WORK_LEAVE_WARNING` and an in-flight or unresolved save still
gives `UNRESOLVED_SAVE_LEAVE_WARNING`.

**Layout.** Desktop renders both views as tables inside a `relative max-h-[70vh] overflow-auto`
scroller with a left-sticky product column and top-sticky header rows (Plan picks adds the site row,
offsetting the column header row with `top-9`); the `relative` keeps the scroller the containing
block of its absolutely positioned screen-reader labels, without which they widened the page.
Below 768px (`matchMedia`, desktop in jsdom) both views switch to product cards with a machine focus
strip, steppers and a summary bar kept above the mobile bottom navigation. Plan picks' own steppers
are no longer part of that breakpoint since issue #1008: its minus/box/plus row renders at every
width, so the cards differ from the matrix only in layout, never in the interaction.

**Tests.** `pick-list.component.plan-picks.spec.ts` (quantity parsing, refresh/retry and stale
responses, every discard confirmation and what Cancel keeps, overrides, skips, totals, filters, focus,
site grouping, suggestions, the departure guard, and the rendered summary and phone cards; and for
issue #1008 the always-visible box and its steppers, their bounds at 0 and `MAXIMUM_PICK_QUANTITY`,
every refused input kept whole with its message and the retained last valid quantity, the blank box
as incomplete input, completion cleared and blocked while a cell is unreadable, and pending text
surviving filters, sorting, mode switching and machine focus; and for issue #1021 the plan written on
every change, restored into a freshly created component with no pick-list read, the departure warning
withheld only for a stored plan and still raised for a refused write and for Record refill work,
every discard clearing the stored copy, a cancelled confirmation changing neither, a trimmed and an
entirely vanished machine list, a stale scope, a restore that lands after the operator has applied a
selection, the `?mode=manual` preselection surviving it, and - for the scope rules above - a stored
plan whose machines the fleet now lists under different machine records refused whole, a run no
machine of which can be identified never stored and still warned about, the displayed plan and its
stored copy discarded when the account, business or support/role-preview context changes, a snapshot
answering for the previous scope neither shown nor stored, and a restoration pending when the scope
changes dropped). `plan-picks-storage.spec.ts` covers the
stored format, the account/business scope and every refused payload - including a malformed or
missing machine identity and a first-format record - plus storage that throws on
read, write and remove; `plan-picks-store.service.spec.ts` covers the eligibility rules - unread and
unavailable access, nobody signed in, a support session, a role preview - the scope token that
invalidates a restoration in flight, what `scopeToken$` publishes, and `save` refusing a plan whose
scope has moved on. `plan-picks-store.spec-helpers.ts` is the in-memory double the
other Pick List specs use.
These sit beside the issue #996 tests in `manual-pick-list.component.spec.ts` (aggregate storage checks
including hidden rows, hidden-entry banner, Clear, the recorded summary, locked entries while
unresolved, and Retry save despite a shortage).

#### Supplier Orders frontend page (issue #387)

Supplier orders moved from a Products-area child view to a dedicated Purchases workflow page,
`SupplierOrdersComponent` (`frontend/inventory-app/src/app/components/purchases`, routed at
`/purchases/orders`). It is a thin consumer of the existing `SupplierOrderService` and the
existing `GET /api/supplierorders` contract: it introduces no new service, DTO, endpoint, or
supplier-order business rule. `GET /api/supplierorders` already returns only active orders
(`Ordered`/`PartiallyReceived`; `Received`, `Cancelled` and - since issue #974 -
`ClosedPartiallyDelivered` are excluded in `EfSupplierOrderStore`),
so the page states on screen that it shows open orders only, and its supplier/reference search and
Ordered/Partially-received status filter are purely client-side presentation filters over that
already-active set, not new query parameters on the endpoint. Listing received, cancelled or completed
orders remains out of scope; it needs a new API contract. The page's Receive/Create Purchase and Cancel
actions are unchanged from the previous Products-area view: Receive navigates to
`/purchases/new?supplierOrderId=<id>` (the existing `PurchaseUploadComponent` prefill workflow, which
since issue #974 asks about the order's outstanding balance before saving) and Cancel calls
`SupplierOrderService.cancel`. Both actions are offered only while the order is one of the two **open**
statuses rather than "not one of the closed ones", so a closed status added later is excluded by default
instead of being offered a write; `ClosedPartiallyDelivered` renders as **Completed — partially delivered**
and, where an order records one, the line table shows an **Undelivered** column beside Outstanding, which
the server supplies as each line's `undeliveredQuantity`.

**Compatibility treatment of the old Products "On Order" entry point.** The Products-area
`ProductOnOrderComponent` (previously routed at `/products/on-order`) was removed rather than kept
as a second, diverging listing of the same active orders: `/products/on-order` is now a `redirectTo`
route alias to `/purchases/orders` in `app.routes.ts`, so an existing bookmark or link still lands on
the (now single) Supplier Orders implementation instead of a stale duplicate. `ProductsShellComponent`'s
"On order" tab links directly to `/purchases/orders`. `PurchaseUploadComponent` navigates back to
`/purchases/orders` (rather than the old `/products/on-order`) after a receipt that started from a
supplier order, and its "Unable to load supplier order" and Cancel links point at the same new page.

#### Shared Add/Edit purchase layout (issue #1029)

Add Purchase and Edit Purchase render one presentational layout, `components/purchases/purchase-form/purchase-form-layout.component.ts`, from the owner-approved Stitch design: Purchase details (supplier, date, title and the receipt control), Purchased items, the collapsible Additional costs and Notes, the Purchase summary and a sticky Cancel / Save purchase bar. Screenshots at 360/390/768/1440px are in `docs/screenshots/issue-1029/`, produced by `frontend/inventory-app/e2e/visual/purchase-form-redesign.visual.ts` against synthetic API answers.

- **Who owns what.** The layout owns presentation state only: which optional sections are expanded, which lines were touched and whether Save was pressed (the touched/submitted validation display). `PurchaseUploadComponent` (Add) and `PurchaseEditFormComponent` (Edit) still own their form object and lines, pass them in by reference, and keep every rule that differs between creating and editing - what a save submits, which GST classifications are sent (Add omits Not classified; Edit sends only changed ones with each stored line's `id`), how the date becomes an instant, and where Cancel goes. Field ids and `data-testid`s are prefixed per form (`editTitle`, `edit-purchase-item`), so both pages keep the ids their tests and the end-to-end suite use.
- **One line-price module.** Every quantity and price change goes through the existing `purchase-line-price.ts` (`enterLineTotal`, `enterUnitCost`, `syncPurchaseLinePrice`), so the last-edited-field rule, the unrounded submitted unit cost and the four-decimal calculated display are unchanged. A line now starts with no product (`productId` 0) and both forms refuse to submit a line without one.
- **Summary figures.** The items subtotal is the existing sum of `round(quantity x unitCost, 2)`; the purchase total adds the entered delivery and package charges (`purchase-receipt-comparison.ts`). The Receipt total is the existing optional `totalAmount`, persisted exactly as before; its Matches receipt / Difference comparison mirrors `PurchaseTotalValidationPolicy` (unrounded item sum plus charges, absolute difference rounded to cents away from zero, `Tolerance` 1.00 deciding only whether the difference is styled as the list's mismatch warning). It is display only and never affects a save. Angular still performs no GST arithmetic: Add says GST is calculated when saved, and Edit shows the saved `gst` block as last saved.
- **Receipt lifecycle.** `PurchaseReceiptFieldComponent` holds no state of its own. On Add the chosen file travels in the existing create request only when the purchase is saved, so preview (a local object URL), replace and remove touch nothing on the server. On Edit, a purchase with a stored document shows it with Preview only (fetched through the authorized `GET /api/purchases/{id}/file`): the API has no replace or delete for a stored document, and this change adds none, so opening or cancelling Edit cannot remove one. For a purchase with none, `PurchaseEditPageComponent` sends the chosen file through the existing `POST /api/purchases/{id}/file` after the `PUT` succeeds; a refused attach is reported and leaves the saved edit in place. Because the router reuses the page between edit URLs, the purchase id, title and chosen file are captured when Save is pressed, and every load and the page's destruction start a new context: a response for an earlier purchase still attaches the file submitted with it to that purchase and reports its outcome by toast, but never changes the purchase now on screen (its saving or error state or chosen receipt) or navigates it away.
- **Shared controls.** `PurchaseProductPickerComponent` is a combobox over the business's own loaded products (name and `unit` only); it closes on Escape, Tab, an outside click or focus leaving the box, so it is never open beside a help panel. The price, GST and receipt-total explanations use the one shared `components/shared/help-toggletip/` component from issue #1016 unchanged (its contract is described under "Shared help toggletip (issues #1015 and #1016)"): each caller passes the full accessible name as `label` ("About unit price") and projects its sentence as content.
- **Unchanged.** Routes, API contracts, permissions, tenant isolation, support-session write blocking, the supplier-order completion dialog and every GST, costing, stock and rounding rule.

#### Purchase edit page (issue #475)

Editing a purchase is a dedicated page, not a row that expands inside the purchases table. The
inline editor the list used to hold is **gone**: `purchase-list.component.{ts,html}` is display and
delete only, holds no edit form, no edit state and no `PUT` request, and its Actions cell's Edit is
an `<a [routerLink]="['/purchases', r.id, 'edit']">` rather than a button that toggled a second
`<tr>`. That is also what makes the list compact again — the saved-figures-exclude-unsaved-edits
note the list rendered while an editor was open (issue #431) no longer exists, because no unsaved
edit can be in the list any more.

Two components sit behind the route, split on the [page composition
boundary](#page-composition-boundary-issue-191):

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `components/purchases/purchase-edit/purchase-edit-page.component.{ts,html}` | The routed page: the `:id` route parameter, the purchase/supplier/product reads, the loading, unavailable and save-error states, the `PurchaseService.update` call, and the navigation back to the list |
| `components/purchases/purchase-edit/purchase-edit-form.component.{ts,html}` | The form itself: its fields, its line-item operations and the request payload it emits through `(saveRequested)`/`(editCancelled)`. It makes no request of its own |

- **Direct loading, by id.** The page resolves `:id` from `ActivatedRoute.paramMap` and reads the
  purchase through the existing authorized `PurchaseService.get` (`GET /api/purchases/{id}`), so a
  bookmarked edit URL, a page refresh and browser Back/Forward between two edit URLs all load the
  right purchase. Nothing is carried in navigation-only state and nothing depends on a list
  component instance still existing. `paramMap` rather than a snapshot is what makes an id change on
  a reused component reload instead of leaving the previous purchase's values on screen.
- **Permissions and tenant isolation are the API's, unchanged.** The route is behind `MsalGuard`
  exactly as every other page is, and `GET`/`PUT /api/purchases/{id}` stay `[Authorize]`d and scoped
  by the `AppDbContext` tenant query filters (see [Tenant ownership](#tenant-ownership-issue-64)).
  Another business's purchase id therefore reaches this page's unavailable state rather than its
  data, and no request this page makes names an owner. The route is not an authorization boundary
  and must not become one.
- **The three non-form states.** A loading state while the read is outstanding (never an empty
  form); a `404` reported as "no longer available" and a failed read reported separately as a
  failure to load, each with a Back to Purchases link and no form at all; and a save refusal shown
  above the form with the API's own message, with every entered value still on the page, so a
  rejected GST classification never looks like a saved one. A save in flight disables Save, and the
  page ignores a second submission, so one purchase cannot be updated twice by a double press.
- **Save and Cancel both return to `/purchases`.** The list reloads on `ngOnInit`, which is how the
  updated values appear. The list carries no filter, sort or paging state, so there is nothing to
  preserve across the round trip and no query parameter or navigation state is used for it; if the
  list ever gains those, this is the one place that would need to carry them.
- **The form moved unchanged.** Title, supplier, purchase date, total amount, the purchased-item
  lines (product for a new line, quantity, unit cost, per-line GST classification, add and remove),
  delivery cost with its GST picker, package cost with its GST picker, and notes are exactly the
  fields and operations the inline editor offered, with the same `name`s, the same `data-testid`s and
  the same validation. Issue #707 then added per-line price entry and the line-price validation this
  form now performs before it emits a payload, and issue #878 made it the two linked Unit price and
  Total price inputs described in
  [Per-line price entry](#per-line-price-entry-total-paid-or-unit-price-issue-707); every other field
  is still the one listed here. Every issue #431 rule still holds and its tests moved with the code: only a
  changed classification is submitted, a stored line travels with its own `id` and keeps its product,
  an absent charge submits no classification, and an unchanged purchase date is resubmitted as the
  stored instant. The GST figures are still the API's alone and are still displayed on the list; this
  page performs no GST arithmetic. Editing a purchase still cannot replace its uploaded document -
  `PUT /api/purchases/{id}` never accepted a file, and this page adds no way to send one. Issue #976
  did not change that: a purchase with **no** document can be given one, but from the Purchases list
  and through its own endpoint, and replacing an existing document stays out of scope (see
  [A purchase's document is optional](#a-purchases-document-is-optional-issue-976)).
- **Breadcrumb.** `/purchases/:id/edit` is a static `Purchases > Edit purchase` entry in
  `layout/breadcrumbs/breadcrumb-routes.ts` (see [Breadcrumbs](#breadcrumbs-issue-457)); the page
  renders no breadcrumb markup of its own and contributes no live label.
- **No unsaved-change guard.** The repository has no unsaved-change protection pattern - no
  `CanDeactivate` guard, no dirty-state service, and `/products/:id/edit` has none either - so this
  page behaves like every other form page: leaving it, by Cancel, by Back or by any other link,
  discards unsaved edits without a prompt. Introducing a prompt here would be a new cross-cutting
  pattern and is deliberately not part of issue #475.

#### Per-line price entry: total paid or unit price (issue #707)

Stock usually arrives in boxes priced per box, so each purchase line on **both** purchase forms -
`components/purchases/purchase-upload.component.{ts,html}` (Add) and
`components/purchases/purchase-edit/purchase-edit-form.component.{ts,html}` (Edit) - shows **both**
of its prices beside its quantity, as two editable inputs next to each other: **Unit price ($)** and
**Total price ($)**. Issue #878 replaced issue #707's price-entry selector and its read-only hint
text with them; there is no mode to choose and no `Line total:`/`Unit cost:` figure under a field.

| Field | What the operator types | What it calculates, into the other field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Total price ($)` | the GST-inclusive amount paid for the whole line (a box price) | the unit cost, `lineTotal / quantity`, displayed to four decimals |
| `Unit price ($)` | the price of one unit | the line total, `round(quantity x unitCost, 2)` |

- **The field typed into last is the entered figure.** `PriceEntryMode` survives as exactly that -
  which of the two prices won - and is set by typing rather than by a selector: typing in Total
  price makes the total the entered figure and the unit cost the calculated one, typing in Unit price
  does the reverse, and typing in the other field afterwards hands the win over again. A change of
  quantity recalculates from whichever field won last: an entered total is spread over the new unit
  count, an entered unit price is multiplied by it.
- **One shared calculation.** `components/purchases/purchase-line-price.ts` holds which field wins
  (`enterLineTotal`/`enterUnitCost`), both directions of the arithmetic, the cent rounding, what each
  field displays (`unitPriceFieldValue`/`totalPriceFieldValue`) and the per-line validation, and both
  forms delegate to it, so Add and Edit cannot drift apart (AGENTS.md § Architecture rules). It is an
  entry convenience over the existing contract: no pack size, units-per-box or carton is modelled,
  which field was typed is not part of any request or any stored row, and a line is still persisted
  and submitted as the quantity and unit cost `PurchaseItemDto` already carried. Purchase GST remains
  the API's alone - these forms still perform no GST arithmetic.
- **The unit cost is submitted as the unrounded quotient.** While the total is the entered figure the
  request carries `lineTotal / quantity` exactly as computed, never rounded to the four decimals the
  Unit price field displays, because that is what makes the saved line's amount reproduce the amount
  entered: $100.00 over 300 units is $0.3333... per unit and `round(300 x 0.3333..., 2)` is $100.00,
  while a unit cost stored as `0.3333` would save $99.99. That is why a calculated figure has a
  **display value separate from the submitted one**: the Unit price field shows `0.3333` while
  `unitCost` stays the quotient, and the Total price field shows a calculated total to the cent
  (`42.00`, not `42`). An entered figure is displayed exactly as it was typed, and only an actual
  edit of a field - never focusing or blurring it - replaces the value behind it, so the rounded
  figure on screen can never become the submitted one. `PurchaseGstPolicy.LineAmount` is unchanged
  and stays the authority on that figure; `PurchaseGstPolicyTests` pins both halves of the
  comparison, and `EfPurchaseStoreTests` pins that the stored `decimal(18,4)` column keeps enough
  precision for the round trip on a real SQLite database.
- **Which field wins when a form opens.** Every new Add Purchase line starts with `Total price`
  winning, including a line prefilled from a supplier order, which opens on the line total its
  recorded unit price implies. A line **already stored** on a purchase opens with `Unit price`
  winning on the edit form, because the unit cost is the figure the purchase actually holds:
  calculating it from a rounded total would make a quantity correction re-cost the line, and a stored
  cost no cent amount divides evenly into could not be reproduced from that total at all. A line
  added during an edit has no stored cost and starts like an Add Purchase line.
- **Nothing is derived until the operator types something.** Opening a form never changes the unit
  cost a line would submit: a prefilled or stored line keeps the unit cost it was read with, and
  opening and saving a purchase with no edit submits the unit costs it was read with. A change of
  quantity or of either amount then recalculates the complementary figure immediately, so neither
  figure is ever shown stale.
- **Validation happens before anything is submitted.** A line needs a whole number of units above
  zero and a finite, non-negative amount in the field that won, and its unit cost must itself be
  finite and non-negative. Clearing the entered field, or an unusable quantity, clears the calculated
  field rather than dividing by zero or leaving a stale figure; each line shows what it is missing,
  and both forms refuse to send the purchase at all - so `NaN`, an infinity and a blank price never
  reach `POST`/`PUT /api/purchases`. The server's own `PurchaseItemFormatPolicy` check is unchanged
  and still has the final say.
- **Out of scope by design.** The purchase-level Total Amount (the invoice total, which also covers
  delivery and package charges), the delivery cost and the package cost are untouched and are still
  entered as plain amounts; the extracted-receipt lines table and the purchases list's own unit-cost
  display are unchanged; and no existing purchase is repriced, backfilled or recosted by either this
  change or issue #878's two linked fields.

#### Supplier product price history and comparison (issue #63)

The Purchasing/Suppliers vertical slice derives a per-product supplier price comparison from actual,
immutable `PurchaseItem.UnitCost` history joined to its owning Purchase's date, title/reference, and
supplier, rather than adding a separate quoted/current-price table: every supplier a
product was ever actually bought from remains visible. `Product` used to carry a `SupplierId` as a
default for ordering, which was never the source of this comparison and which issue #787 removed
(see [A product carries no supplier](#a-product-carries-no-supplier-issue-787)); the purchase history
this comparison reads *is* now the only record of who a product is bought from, and it is the better
one, because a product bought from whoever is cheapest this month never had one supplier to store.
`Inventory.Domain.Purchases.SupplierPriceComparisonPolicy`
is the one authoritative calculation: it selects the lowest and most recent recorded unit cost with
deterministic tie-breaks (lowest-cost ties break to the earliest occurrence; latest-date ties break to
the higher purchase item id), computes the absolute/percentage difference between them - leaving the
percentage unset rather than dividing by a zero lowest cost - and returns every recorded entry
newest-first without discarding a tied record. `Inventory.Application.Purchases.GetProductPriceComparison`
is the use case; `Inventory.Application.Purchases.IProductPurchasePriceHistoryProvider` is the narrow
port a product's actual Purchase-item history is read through, implemented by
`Inventory.Infrastructure.Persistence.EfProductPurchasePriceHistoryProvider` (API-owned until issue
#309 moved the adapter family beside the `AppDbContext` it reads). `ProductsController`'s
`GET /api/products/{id}/price-history` and the Angular `app-product-price-history` feature component
(composed into the product-edit page's at-a-glance summary and "View price history" drill-down, per
[Page composition boundary](#page-composition-boundary-issue-191)) only fetch and present this result.

This comparison is historical/quoted guidance, never a substitute for AVCO or a
live supplier quote: it never feeds inventory costing, and a supplier-order creation flow that shows it
for reference must not let it silently overwrite an entered order price/cost. A Purchase with no
supplier recorded stays visible in the comparison and history with an explicit null/"None" source
rather than being omitted.

**The same facts for the whole catalogue at once: `GET api/products/purchase-cost-summary` (issue
#788, B of parent #786).** The product screens need every product's last and cheapest cost together,
and one `price-history` request per product is an N+1 against the purchase history. The bulk answer is
`Inventory.Application.Purchases.ListProductPurchaseCostSummaries`, which reads the history in one
query through the `IProductPurchaseCostFactsProvider` port the profitability report already uses and
then applies **this same `SupplierPriceComparisonPolicy.Evaluate`** per product. It selects nothing
itself, which is the whole design: there is no third last/cheapest formula, and
